correctness.rationale: For every k>=3 the required degree imbalance is exactly +/-1 on complementary first/last-pair types. An unrestricted path from each negative vertex cannot reach a positive vertex before its first equal pair is shifted into the prefix. The explicit first/last-equal-pair bijection realizes all these individually sharp lower bounds simultaneously while preserving the no-triple-run constraint. The balanced strongly connected multigraph has an Eulerian tour. The H_m run-composition count and induction give overhead 2(F_(k-1)-1). Direct standalone verifier checks k3..18, independent assignment k3..11, exhaustive shorter hosts k3..5; finite checks are corroboration only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A universal cycle would imply zero overhead. The compulsory graph here has 2F_{k-3} sources and sinks for k>=4 and hence positive overhead. A maximal nonrepeating constrained de Bruijn sequence is not a minimum repeat-allowing host covering every linearly admissible word. General algorithms for Eulerian graphs do not by themselves imply the Lucas closed form.

value.rationale: The exact minimum length of a periodic test sequence covering every linearly permitted run-two window is a natural invariant relevant to constrained coding and sequence test generation. The optimum is nontrivial since the compulsory digraph is unbalanced for k>=4 and host windows were allowed to violate the constraint. The first/last-equal-pair matching gives an explicit all-orders optimal construction and a forbidden-free host; Lucas growth and limiting relative overhead quantify unavoidable redundancy. This is not a mere renaming of a known table or an arbitrary parameter slice.
